keys.short: Free-form label (logs/report titles only — not used for lookup).

Optional pre-trade `RiskGate` limits (runprofile-wiring-step2). The SAME `risk` schema AND the SAME compile-checked converter (`vike_model::ProfileRisk::to_risk_limits`) `vike-core`'s `ProfileRun` uses for paper/live — so a limit proven here (via `ProfileBacktest::validate` + a real `OrderBrokerSimulator` denial) carries unchanged into paper and live, rather than being re-derived by a parallel converter that could drift. Absent (the default) ⇒ `vike_simulator::StrategyEngineConfig::risk_limits` stays `None` ⇒ byte-identical to every profile written before this field existed: `engine` today has no `leverage` knob either, so `risk` is the ONLY way a harness profile arms the gate at all (`vike_simulator::OrderBrokerSimulator::build_risk_gate`'s `(None, None) => None` arm).

Optional PARAMETER-SEARCH grid: each key is a `strategy.params` field name, each value an array of TOML values to cross-product over (expansion lives in `super::paramscan::expand_paramscan`). Absent or empty means "not a parameter search".

Optional anchored WALK-FORWARD config — the `paramscan` sibling: present means this profile can ALSO be run through `crate::walkforward::runner::run_walkforward` over `walkforward.n_splits` out-of-sample windows. Absent (the default) is byte-identical to every profile written before this field existed, and `run_backtest`/`run_paramscan` ignore the section entirely — exactly as they ignore a `sweep` table they were not asked to expand.

Optional REMAP of the series the strategy reads by name (decision 0271): each row is `"<the name the strategy's code writes>" = "<the series to read instead>"`, both in the input grammar, `VENUE:SYMBOL:INTERVAL` or `LANE:VENUE:SYMBOL:INTERVAL` (a user's CSV import is the lane `user-<label>`). A name the code writes works without a row, so absent (the default) reads every input as its code names it, and a profile written before this table is byte-identical. A row naming no input the strategy reads is refused when the run builds it (`crate::data_plan::resolve_inputs`).
Single-venue form: the one venue every entry of `Self::symbols` lives under. Mutually exclusive with `Self::series`.
Single-venue form: the symbols to load under `Self::venue`. Mutually exclusive with `Self::series`.
Cross-venue form (`[data.series]`): one entry per series, each naming its own `venue`, `symbol` and (tick mode only) lane `kind`. Mutually exclusive with `Self::venue`/`Self::symbols`.
Bare epoch-ms integer (as a string) or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH` UTC — see `ProfileBacktest::range`.
Same format as `from`.

How much history the strategy's indicators need before the run's FIRST tradeable event — a bar/event count (`"200bars"`) or, in bar mode, a duration (`"7d"`) the base `Self::interval` divides into one. Absent (the default) is byte-identical to every profile written before this key existed: the gate stays exactly `Strategy::warmup()`.

Opt-in INTRABAR DETAIL TAPE: a per-symbol series FINER than `Self::interval`, loaded over the same range and bucketed into each coarse step, against which every order is resolved while the strategy keeps deciding on the coarse timeframe. Absent (the default) is byte-identical to every profile written before this key existed. BAR MODE ONLY.

PLAN-THEN-APPLY: resolve this profile's whole data slice, report what the store holds for it, and EXIT without computing. Absent (the default) is byte-identical to every profile written before this key existed.

ARM THE COVERAGE GATE: refuse (or warn on) a run whose window the store does not cover. Absent (the default) is byte-identical to every profile written before this key existed — the run loads whatever is there and says nothing.
How much of the window `Self::require_coverage` tolerates missing in ONE span, as a fixed duration (`"1d"`, `"4h"`, `"900000"` ms). Absent = ZERO tolerance: any missing span at all is a finding.
What `Self::require_coverage` DOES about a finding: `"refuse"` (the default — nothing runs), `"warn"` (the findings are logged and the run proceeds unchanged), or `"run"` (the gate is inert).

POINT-IN-TIME UNIVERSE MEMBERSHIP — the survivorship defence. `"declared"` (the default, byte-identical: the symbol list is taken verbatim), `"covered"` (a member whose tape does not span the window is NAMED and the run proceeds), or `"strict"` (that run is REFUSED).

Read the bars from a `source=` LANE of the store instead of the venue's own candles: a declared lane (`"aggtrades"`, `"tardis"`) or a user's, `"user-<label>"` (decision 0268). Absent (the default) reads the venue's own candles, byte-identical to every profile written before this key. Bar mode only, and never with `Self::file`.

Read the bars from a CSV FILE on the box that runs the backtest, without importing it (decision 0268): ONE series, its columns found by header name, through the decoder the `csv-bars` import uses, so a file this reads is a file the import takes. A relative path resolves against the profile's own directory. Bar mode only, and never with `Self::source`.

How `Self::file`'s cells are written, when not the plain form (`,` between fields, `.` as the decimal mark, no thousands separator, integer epoch times): the explicit options a regional export needs, e.g. `{ delimiter = ";", decimal = ",", thousands = "space", time = "DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm", tz = "Europe/Moscow" }`. Nothing reads the machine's locale, and a file in a regional form read without these is refused naming the option to set. Only with `file`.

The currency `engine.cash` and every other money value of this profile (`engine.fee.min`, `engine.fee.per_share`, the risk ceilings) are WRITTEN in, and the report is READ in: a fiat code such as JPY, in any case. Absent (the default) = the dollar, which is what every profile written before this key was, byte-identical.

The CONVERSION PAIR of each quote currency that is not the ledger's (decision 0243 phase 2): `QUOTE = "<series>"`, the series in the input grammar (`VENUE:SYMBOL:INTERVAL`, or `LANE:VENUE:SYMBOL:INTERVAL` for a lane such as a CSV import's `user-<label>`; one part, `INTERVAL`, is the run's own symbol): `JPY = "dukascopy:USDJPY:1h"`, `USDT = "user-coinbase:coinbase:USDT-USD:1d"`. The pair's SYMBOL says which way its price points against `Self::account_currency`: `QUOTE`+`LEDGER` as it stands, `LEDGER`+`QUOTE` inverted (`vike_model::AccountPerQuoteLeg::of_pair_name`). Refused at load: a key that is no currency code, the ledger itself or a currency named twice, a series the grammar does not read, and a symbol that names neither way round (`resolve_conversions`).

The ACCOUNT's margin mode, in `vike_model::MarginMode`'s own words. `"cash"` is a SPOT account: every symbol the run trades takes the live engine's spot rule (`vike_simulator::StrategyEngineConfig::cash_symbols`), so a sell past the long less the sells already out is refused in its words ("a spot account cannot sell more than it holds…") and lands in the result's `dropped`. `"cross"` WRITTEN OUT is a margin account for every symbol (a sell past the long opens a short), what every profile written before the spot rule ran. ABSENT reads the rule off each series' name (the spot rule, owner 2026-11-11: one spot law in live, paper and backtest): a spot pair takes it, a derivative does not (`super::cash_symbols`). `"isolated"` is refused at load (vike does not run isolated margin yet), as is any other word (`super::margin_mode`).

The run's slippage: `engine.slippage` with ONE `model` (`none`, `percent`, `ticks`, `market_impact`), the one place a profile states it (`ProfileEngineSlippage`'s module doc). Absent (the default) is no slippage, what every profile without one always ran.

Charge each series the stored market `funding` series (`vike-cli data hist fetch <venue>:<symbol>:funding` writes it) on the VENUE'S OWN schedule, the stored timestamps, never a fixed interval: each funding instant is charged once on the position held AT it (the one from before that bar's fills; on the tick lane, before the first tick at or after it), at the venue's published mark when stored (binance, deribit's index) else the bar's open or the tick's price, an inverse contract in its settle coin; deribit's continuous accrual is charged per minute of its hour (`crate::harness::run::FundingAccrual`). A funding-reading strategy reads the SUM of the rates due by each bar on its `Bar.funding` (`crate::harness::window_join_funding`).

Opt-in feed-latency replay (see `crate::tick_replay::TickReplayConfig::feed_latency`): deliver ticks to the strategy in recorded ARRIVAL (`local_timestamp`) order instead of venue order, while order matching stays on venue `ts`. Absent (the default `false`) = today's venue-ordered replay, byte-identical. TICK MODE ONLY — a bar has no `local_timestamp`, so a profile that sets this with `data.kind = "bar"` is rejected by `ProfileBacktest::validate` rather than silently ignored.

Opt-in ORDER latency (see `vike_simulator::LatencyModelKind`): a fixed entry-leg delay in MILLISECONDS on every strategy order action (place / modify / cancel). The maker's quotes, re-prices and pulls only reach the matching engine `order_latency_ms` after it decides them, so it cannot react within one tick — the missing clock skew that otherwise lets a maker enter and exit in the same instant. `0` (the default) = zero latency, byte-identical. TICK MODE ONLY (only `run_ticks` arms the latency gate; the bar lane and vector kernel never consult it).

Opt-in FILL-notification latency (the response leg, see `vike_simulator::LatencyModelKind`): a fixed delay in MILLISECONDS before the strategy LEARNS of a fill. The fill books at the real time (equity/PnL are exact), but the strategy-visible shadow position (`vike_model::OrderBroker::position`) does not advance until `fill_latency_ms` later — so a maker that polls its inventory cannot react (place its exit) inside that gap. Models the "time to realise you're filled" half of a real round-trip reaction. `0` (the default) = off, byte-identical. TICK MODE ONLY.

Opt-in tick-lane fill-model override: `"l2book"` (the ONE accepted value; case-insensitive, like `Self::queue_model`) selects the depth-capped `vike_simulator::FillModelKind::L2Book` (a resting order fills only up to the DISPLAYED book depth; when the within-limit depth cannot cover its size it RESTS rather than filling size the market never showed), vs the default L1 spread-crossing `Tick` model (fills the full size at the quote). Absent ⇒ `Tick`, byte-identical. Any OTHER value is a fail-fast `HarnessError::Validation` at load (`ProfileEngine::fill_model_kind`, the mirror of the `Self::queue_model` rule) — a typo like `"l2_book"` must not silently select the optimistic `Tick` model and undo the depth-cap realism knob. TICK MODE ONLY. Pair with no `engine.slippage` (the book walk IS the slippage).
Stop-verb release timing (see `vike_simulator::StrategyEngineConfig::emulator_release_stops`).

Opt-in fee SCHEDULE (port backlog G7) — the shapes a flat `Self::fee_rate` cannot express. Absent with a zero `fee_rate` (the default) = the venue table of each symbol's own fee lane, as the Studio prices it (a slice over two lanes pays each symbol its own row, never zero). Setting BOTH is a validation error: two cost models would be configured and only one could win.

Opt-in binary-resolution settlement (port backlog G6): builds the `vike_simulator::StrategyEngineConfig::resolution` source + `resolution_end_timestamp` the engine has always consumed. Absent (the default) = no settlement source, byte-identical.

Opt-in QUEUE-POSITION fill model for the tick lane (see `vike_simulator::QueueModelKind`): a resting limit — INCLUDING a tagged MAKER quote — no longer fills the instant price touches it, but only once a taker TRADE has consumed the size AHEAD of it in the FIFO queue (seeded from the replayed L2 book's size at that price, or the last L1 quote, or `Self::queue_seed_depth`). This is the realistic passive-maker fill: a quote earns the spread only when flow actually hits it, with partial fills on the trade's excess over the front. Absent (the default) = the frozen simple-crossing fill (`fill_tagged`), byte-identical. TICK MODE ONLY — the queue lane is consulted exclusively by `run_ticks`, so a bar-mode profile setting it is rejected by `ProfileBacktest::validate` (the mirror of the `feed_latency` rule). Values (case-insensitive): `"risk_averse"` (the conservative bound — front shrinks only on hard evidence), `"prob_power"` / `"prob_power:N"` (probabilistic, `f(x)=x^N`, default `N=1`), `"prob_log"`. For a real maker backtest feed the TRADE tape (and, for true size-ahead seeding, the BOOK).

Fallback front-of-queue depth (in size units) seeded when neither the replayed L2 book nor an L1 quote gives a size at a resting order's price — see `vike_simulator::QueueModelKind`. Only consulted when `Self::queue_model` is set. Absent ⇒ `0.0` (a quote with no observed size-ahead fills on the first at-price trade).

Minimum-hold floor in MS for the queued lane (`vike_simulator::StrategyEngineConfig::queue_min_hold_ms`): a position-reducing (closing) fill is deferred until this long after the position opened, so the backtest can't fabricate a sub-second maker round-trip. Only consulted when `Self::queue_model` is set. Absent ⇒ `0` (off). Calibrate from real MM flip times (Polymarket BTC-5m ≈ 2s p10).

Equity-curve density for the tick lane (see `vike_simulator::EquitySampling`) — the SWEEP knob for a very long tape. The curve is two `Vec`s grown 16 bytes per priced tick, so a 100M-tick replay carries 1.6 GB of samples per run whether or not anything reads them.

Higher timeframes synthesised from the base bar stream, look-ahead safe: a coarse bar becomes visible only once its window has fully elapsed. Each entry is an `vike_marketdata::interval::interval_ms` spelling (`"4h"`, `"1d"`). Absent (the default) registers nothing, which is byte-identical to before this key existed.
Admit a fill only when the shared cash pool can fund it. Default `false`, which is what every profile written before this key did.

Add the closed-trade block to the report: one lot per entry fill, exits closing the oldest first, every row net of both commissions, with its trades-analysis statistics in all, long and short columns, the account-wide figures and the list of trades. Default `true`; `false` leaves the block out, as a report written before 2026-11-10 lacks it.

The yearly risk-free rate the closed-trade block's monthly Sharpe and Sortino subtract, a fraction (`0.03` is 3%). Absent: the reference's 2%. Read only where `closed_trades` is on; it prices nothing.

How the closed-trade block books a lot's entry commission when the lot is closed in parts: `false` (the default) shares it by quantity among the rows that close it, `true` books the whole of it on the first row that closes any of it (`vike_analytics::closed_trades::TradeClosedLedgerOptions::whole_entry_fee`). The two agree once a lot is closed whole. Read only where `closed_trades` is on, and refused without it; it prices nothing.

WHEN a multi-symbol step is decided — `"sequential"` (absent = the default, byte-identical to every profile written before this key) or `"simultaneous"`. Resolved by `decide_mode`, which owns the unknown-spelling refusal; the ARGUMENT is in `vike_simulator::DecideMode`, and this doc deliberately does not restate it.
Maintenance-margin RATE (a fraction of adverse notional), folded as `|size| · adverse · multiplier · maint_margin` by the liquidation watchdog.

Equity cushion held above the maintenance requirement before the watchdog liquidates. ⚠ Defaults to `0.10` to match `StrategyEngineConfig::default()` — a bare `#serde(default)` would give `0.0` and silently change every profile that omits the key.

Opt-in stress knob. ⚠ `true` selects the retired TOTAL-WIPE liquidation model — once `eq_adv <= maint_margin * notional_adv` at the intrabar adverse marks, it force-closes the WHOLE account (bar mode, `StrategyEngine::check_liquidation`) / the triggering symbol in full (tick mode, `StrategyEngine::check_liquidation_tick`). `false` (the default) runs the shared LEAN law (`vike_model::cross_liquidation_plan`) instead: PARTIAL, losers-first liquidation with the `liquidation_buffer` grace line — the opposite of a total wipe. Despite its name, `true` is the CRUDER model, not the gentler one.

Opt-in margin call (`ShortfallCover`, whose doc is the rule): the account against its own long and short margin rates, a position it cannot carry cut by a multiple of the shortfall, and a fill it cannot margin refused whole. Absent (the default) leaves every fill and the liquidation above as they were. ⚠ BAR MODE ONLY, and it REPLACES the `maint_margin` liquidation, so `ProfileBacktest::validate` refuses it beside a `maint_margin` or `venue_style_liquidation`, and on a tick profile.

Participation cap: the fraction of the EVENT's own volume any one fill may take. `None` (the default) means uncapped, which is what every profile did before this key — and which lets a backtest "trade" more than the market traded.
Ceiling on concurrently open positions. ⚠ `0` is the engine's UNLIMITED, not "none" — it is the default, and it is what every profile written before this key did.
Ceiling on concurrently open LONG positions. ⚠ `0` means unlimited, as above.
Ceiling on concurrently open SHORT positions. ⚠ `0` means unlimited, as above.

Contract multiplier applied to every symbol without its own row in `Self::multipliers`. ⚠ Defaults to `1.0`, matching `StrategyEngineConfig::default()` — a bare `#serde(default)` would give `0.0` and zero every position's notional.
Per-symbol contract multipliers, e.g. `ES = 50.0`. A `BTreeMap` rather than a `HashMap` because the engine takes an ordered `Vec` and a run must not depend on hash order.

The run's own leverage. ⚠ Distinct from `risk max_leverage`, which reaches the same gate through `ProfileRisk::initial_margin_requirement` but is a CEILING — this is what the run uses, that is what it may not exceed.
Clamp an order down to what `Self::leverage` allows instead of rejecting it.

Variation-settlement cadence in milliseconds — how often open-position profit is realised into cash instead of accruing. `None` (the default) never settles, which is what every profile did before this key.
Defer an order that falls outside its symbol's trading session instead of filling it. Deferrals are already counted and already reach the report as `BacktestResult::session_deferrals`.

How a strategy's requested size becomes an order size (`vike_analytics::sizing::PositionSizer`, the WealthLab PosSizer port). `None` (the default) passes the request through unchanged (`vike_analytics::sizing::PositionSizerPassThrough`) — what every profile did before this key existed (`StrategyEngine::new` installs it whenever `StrategyEngineConfig::sizer` is `None`).

The simulator's in-bar fill rules (`InBarRules`, whose doc is each rule's law): how one bar's walk meets the resting orders. Absent (the default) = every rule off, byte-identical to every profile written before this table. BAR MODE ONLY, refused on a tick profile and beside the shared-cash lane for the rules that walk a bar (`ProfileBacktest::validate`).

The law a TAGGED plain limit fills by (`QuotesConfig`): `optimistic = true` is the simulator's maker law, `false` the ordinary limit law every other resting order fills by. Absent (the default) is what the strategy file's header declares (`strategy optimistic_quotes`: on for the makers that quoted on the simulator's maker lane), off for a file that declares nothing. Both lanes. The realism stamp names the law the run used (`engine.quotes`).

The strategy file: its path under the project's `strategies/` folder (`trend/momentum.rs`). A `.rhai` file runs in this process; a `.rs` file runs in a sandboxed child process. The one selection key of the backtest and the daemon profile.
per-order minimum quantity floor (venue lot-size grid); checked on the lot-rounded qty.

`risk max_notional_per_order` — the per-order notional cap the pre-trade gate evaluates on every order this engine admits, whatever its origin (strategy-emitted, control-socket-originated, reconcile-originated), but **a position-covered reduce**, which passes it and stays judged by `max_total_exposure`. It lands verbatim in `RiskLimits::max_notional_per_order` and is denied as `over-max-notional`.

`risk max_total_exposure` — cap on **ONE SYMBOL's** projected open notional at **ONE VENUE**, in the account's quote currency. Despite the name it is NOT an account-wide, cross-symbol or cross-venue total: it lands verbatim in `RiskLimits::max_total_exposure`, whose doc is the authority on the scope, on why the name is kept, and on the test that pins it. Size it for a SINGLE instrument — an operator who sizes it for a whole book of N symbols gets an N× weaker cap than they wrote.
throttle window (ms); only active when `max_orders_per_window` is set

THE leverage knob (>= 1.0), e.g. `10.0` ⇒ 10x. Arms the pre-trade buying-power check by converting to `RiskLimits::initial_margin_requirement` (`1.0 / max_leverage`) — see `ProfileRisk::initial_margin_requirement` and the module doc's "One leverage concept, one name". Omitted ⇒ the buying-power lane stays off here (a live mount then applies its own conservative 1× rescue).
LEAN free-buying-power haircut on equity, `[0.0, 1.0)`
Number of out-of-sample windows — window form (a), the one that existed first.
Window form (b)/(c) — the TRAIN window's length, as a `vike_model::time::parse_span` duration (`"12mo"`, `"90d"`, `"5000bars"`). Mutually exclusive with `Self::n_splits`; requires `Self::test`.
Window form (b)/(c) — the VALIDATION window's length. Required with `Self::train`.
How far each window advances. Absent ⇒ equal to `Self::test`, which tiles the validation windows edge to edge.
Bars dropped BETWEEN train and test, so `test_start - train_end == purge` exactly.

The minimum gap AFTER a validation window before the next one may start. A window whose `test_start` falls inside the zone is DROPPED, not moved — moving it would make `Self::step` mean something other than what was written. Same duration-form-only rule as `Self::purge`, and the same ROUNDS-UP rule.

Which search each window runs on its OWN training half — the knob that chooses between the two walk-forward protocols. Absent or `"none"` is the CONTROL (`WalkforwardWindowSearch::None`): every window trades the profile's own `strategy.params`, which is the fixed-parameter walk this section has always described. `"sweep"` — named for the table it expands — scores this profile's `sweep` grid on each window's train half and carries only the winner onto its validation half.

The TRAIN-window shape (`WalkforwardMode`): absent or `"anchored"` is the expanding window every split trains from bar 0; `"rolling"` trains on the ONE chunk immediately preceding the window. Case-insensitive and trimmed (`Self::walk_mode`), unknown values refused at load.

How a window SCORES its candidates when `Self::search` runs one: any of the four `RankMetric` names the sweep's own `--rank-by` takes (`"sharpe"` | `"return"` | `"max_dd"` | `"equity"`, case-insensitive), defaulting to `RankMetric::default`. Consulted only when a search actually runs — the control scores nothing.
Between fields: `","` (the default), `";"` or `"tab"`.
The decimal mark: `"."` (the default) or `","`.
Between thousands: absent (none, the default), `"space"`, `"."` or `","`; never the decimal mark or the delimiter.
`"epoch"` (the default: an integer epoch in s, ms or µs) or a text time's pattern of `YYYY`, `MM`, `DD`, `HH`, `mm`, `ss` and `SSS`, each that many digits: `"DD.MM.YYYY HH:mm"`.
The zone of a text time: `"UTC"` (the default), a fixed offset `"+03:00"`, or an IANA name such as `"Europe/Berlin"`. A wall-clock time the zone passed twice or never is refused.
Which model prices a fill's slippage: `none`, `percent`, `ticks` or `market_impact`.
`percent`: the fraction of the price a fill moves against the trader (`0.0005` is 0.05%).
`ticks`: how many ticks a fill moves against the trader. Every fill no limit bounds pays it (a market, stop or trailing fill, the protective stop, a forced close); a limit fill pays none.
`ticks`: the price one tick is, in the series' own quote units (`0.01`).
`market_impact`: a constant fraction of the price every fill pays beside the impact (absent: none).

`market_impact`: the execution horizon, in this run's periods (bars, or trade prints in tick mode, `vike_simulator::ImpactModelAlmgrenChriss::exec_time`). Absent: `1.0`. ⚠ It scales the TEMPORARY term only, so it cannot move an L2-lane charge: `Self::gamma` can.

`market_impact`: the rolling sigma and volume lookback, in bars (trade prints in tick mode). Absent: `vike_simulator::DEFAULT_IMPACT_WINDOW`, a trading month of daily bars, so a tick profile should set it.
`market_impact`: the permanent-impact coefficient. Absent: the published `vike_simulator::AC_GAMMA`. The one lever an L2-lane charge has, and a linear one.
`market_impact`: the temporary-impact coefficient. Absent: the published `vike_simulator::AC_ETA`. It moves the bar and L1-tick lanes; an L2 fill that walked a book already paid this half.
Which `vike_model::FeeSchedule` shape this table describes: `"probability_scaled"` | `"per_share_with_floor"` | `"percent_of_underlying"` | `"percent_maker_taker"` | `"venue"` | `"free"`.
`probability_scaled`: the TAKER fraction of the `p(1−p)`-scaled share count.
`probability_scaled`: the MAKER fraction, before any rebate.

`probability_scaled`: the maker's rebate as a share of the EQUIVALENT TAKER fee, so a zero `maker_rate` with a positive share is a NEGATIVE maker commission (a rebate — the sign convention on `vike_model::FeeSchedule`).
`per_share_with_floor`: the per-SHARE fee. REQUIRED by that kind.

`per_share_with_floor`: the per-order MINIMUM. REQUIRED by that kind, and required deliberately — an absent floor defaults to no floor, which is the flat-rate behaviour the whole shape exists to escape. Write `min = 0.0` to assert there is genuinely none.

`per_share_with_floor`: the maximum fraction of trade value the fee may reach. Optional — absent is `0.0`, which `FeeSchedule::commission` treats as NO ceiling (it caps only on a positive notional bound), so omitting it charges the uncapped per-share-or-floor figure. That default is safe in the direction that matters: it can only over-charge.
`percent_of_underlying`: basis points of the UNDERLYING notional. REQUIRED by that kind.

`percent_of_underlying`: the cap, as a fraction of the PREMIUM notional (Deribit's real rule caps the underlying term at 12.5 % of the premium). REQUIRED, and a non-positive value is REFUSED rather than read as "no cap": `FeeSchedule::commission` on this shape is `min(bps × premium, cap × premium)`, so a zero cap makes the whole commission zero — the silent free backtest, wearing a configured fee model.
`percent_maker_taker`: maker basis points of quote-notional. At least one of this and `Self::taker_bps` is required; the other defaults to `0.0`.
`percent_maker_taker`: taker basis points of quote-notional. See `Self::maker_bps`.

`venue`: which venue's published schedule to cost the run at. REQUIRED by that kind, and it is not inferred from `data` — `StrategyEngineConfig::fee_schedule` is ONE schedule for the whole run, so on a cross-venue `[data.series]` slice there is no single right answer to infer and naming it is the operator asserting which venue's book this run is priced at.

`venue`: which SYMBOL selects the venue's fee LANE. Absent (the normal case) resolves from the run's own series on `Self::venue`, which is what keeps the `.P` suffix from being typed twice — see `ProfileEngineFee::build_for` for the two ways that resolution refuses.
`venue`, polymarket only: take the verified 2026 V2 fee regime (`vike_venues::POLYMARKET_V2_FEE_CURVE`, via `vike_venues::fee_schedule_for_with_pm_curve`) instead of the registry's `Free`.
currently only `"binary_outcome"`

Seconds from a window's open (`sts`) to its resolution. Defaults to `vike_model::fair::UPDOWN_WINDOW_SECS` (300). NOTE the symbol GRAMMAR is independent of this: `TokenId::parse` pins `sts` to a multiple of `UPDOWN_WINDOW_SECS`, so a different `window_secs` moves the payout TIME without redefining the grid.
Optional `slug,winning_index` CSV. Relative paths resolve against the profile file's own directory (`ProfileBacktest::base_dir`), not the CWD.
Optional inline `slug = winning_index` table. Merged over `path`'s rows.

Explicit override for `vike_simulator::StrategyEngineConfig::resolution_end_timestamp` (epoch-ms or `YYYY-MM-DDTHH`). Absent = the LATEST resolution among the run's own series (`max(sts) + window_secs`), which is what pins the end-of-run sweep to the window rather than to the `RESOLUTION_PROBE_SENTINEL`.
The multiple of the just-enough size a call closes: `4.0` is what the measured reference does, `1.0` closes just enough.
The margin a long must carry, a fraction of its value at the mark (`0.2` is 20%, `1.0` all of it). `0` never calls or refuses a long.
`Self::margin_long` for a short.
The instrument's quantity step the just-enough size floors to (`0.00001` for BTCUSDT). Absent: `0`, which floors nothing.

One of `"pass_through"` | `"fixed_dollar"` | `"fixed_shares"` | `"percent_equity"` | `"percent_volatility"` | `"max_risk_percent"` | `"portfolio_heat"` | `"drawdown_throttle"` — every concrete `vike_analytics::sizing::PositionSizer` this crate ships and nothing else (`Self::build`).
`vike_analytics::sizing::PositionSizerFixedDollar::amount` — fixed cash notional per entry. Required for `"fixed_dollar"`.
`vike_analytics::sizing::PositionSizerFixedShares::shares` — fixed share/contract count per entry. Required for `"fixed_shares"`.

The knob `"percent_equity"` / `"percent_volatility"` / `"max_risk_percent"` each read as their own fraction of equity (target notional, ATR-risk budget, and stop-risk budget respectively — see `vike_analytics::sizing`'s doc on each). Required for those three kinds.
`vike_analytics::sizing::PositionSizerPortfolioHeat::max_heat` — total open-risk cap as a fraction of equity. Required for `"portfolio_heat"`.
`vike_analytics::sizing::PositionSizerDrawdownThrottle::sensitivity`. Required for `"drawdown_throttle"`.
`vike_analytics::sizing::PositionSizerDrawdownThrottle::floor`. Required for `"drawdown_throttle"`.

The wrapped sizer for `"portfolio_heat"` / `"drawdown_throttle"` — required for those two kinds (`Self::build` refuses their absence), and REFUSED under every other kind, which reads it nowhere: a base under a scalar kind would run one sizer while the profile read as a chain. Boxed because `ProfileEngineSizer` nests itself — see `MAX_SIZER_DEPTH` for the bound on how far.

Walk every bar along its path: the open, the nearer extreme, the farther extreme, the close (each bar of `data.detail_interval` so, in turn, when the profile states one), every fill stamped with the bar.
A market order placed on a bar fills at that bar's close instead of the next open, and every order resting then meets that close too.

Resting orders fill in the order the price reaches their levels: each stretch of a bar's walk is cut at every level, and a gap past several fills market orders, then entries, then exits, each from the lowest level. Pair it with `path_walk` (without a walk a bar has one stretch).
The order of the book: market orders first, a new buy ahead of the first resting sell, then the order they were placed in; without it every new order goes last.
A lone protective stop that the next open gaps through fills even after an entry at that open reversed the position, opening its size the other way.
A trailing order placed in reaction to a fill starts watching its activation from that point of the bar, not from the previous bar's close.
A reduce-only order may be placed while nothing is held to reduce; it is checked when it fills instead.

`true`: a limit placed by tag, neither reduce-only nor triggered, fills by the MAKER LAW, in its own pass, whole at the touch, outside the volume cap, the fill-time caps, the in-bar rules and the staleness wait, and its end reaches no order-event hook; `false`: by the ordinary limit law. Untagged orders and every other kind keep their law either way.
